blocks.text:
# Weekly CLI-coverage gardener (issue #177 follow-up, reworked by #927):
# re-measures the terminal/PTY integration suites' coverage of lib/src/cli/**
# and, when it grew, files/updates an issue assigned to ai-teammate asking
# for the baseline raise. The baseline itself NO LONGER auto-commits: every
# bump of scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt lands only through a reviewed PR
# whose per-PR ratchet gate (gh-1005: ci.yml's pty-integration-linux leg,
# the single hosted-linux PTY leg) passes green, and
# each bump must be traceable to a merged PTY test with real frame
# assertions (#927 contract). The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py)
# still enforces the committed floor — coverage can only ratchet UP, a
# silent regression in terminal-test coverage reddens nightly.
name: CLI coverage gardener

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '53 4 * * 1' # Monday, after the shard rebalance
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  measure-and-file:
    name: Measure CLI coverage, file raise-to-X issue if higher
    # gh-1005: measure on the SAME environment the per-PR ratchet measures —
    # ubuntu-24.04-arm (pure-dart job per the runner-split note; OS-identical
    # line hits to the x64 queue).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Run PTY/CLI integration suites with coverage
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
          OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage

      - run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: File coverage-growth issue when measured exceeds baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          measured=$(python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --print | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          baseline=$(cat scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt)
          echo "measured=$measured baseline=$baseline"
          if ! python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$measured') > float('$baseline') else 1)"; then
            echo "No growth — baseline stays $baseline"
            exit 0
          fi
          title="raise coverage to $measured"
          body="$(printf 'Weekly CLI-coverage gardener measured **%s**%% on lib/src/cli/** — above the committed floor of **%s**%% (scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt).\n\nPer the #927 contract the baseline never auto-commits: land the raise through a reviewed PR that\n- updates scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt to %s,\n- passes the per-PR pty-integration-linux ratchet gate green, and\n- traces every bump to a merged PTY test with real frame assertions.\n' "$measured" "$baseline" "$measured")"
          number=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --search "in:title \"raise coverage to\"" --json number,createdAt --jq 'sort_by(.createdAt) | map(.number) | last // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$number" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "updated issue #$number"
          else
            # The #927 AC wants the raise-to-X issue assigned to ai-teammate;
            # keep the measured number alive even when the login is not
            # assignable (renamed/removed) — file unassigned as a fallback.
            gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --assignee ai-teammate --title "$title" --body "$body" ||
              gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "filed raise-to-$measured issue"
          fi

- name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):

      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          # The installer writes version.txt into the bundle; mirror it so
          # `fa --version` from the AOT binary reports the real version
          # (the _packageVersion() fallback chain reads bundle/version.txt).
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # PR runs stamp from git describe (falls back to the short sha
          # on shallow checkouts); release runs get the exact tag from the
          # release binaries job.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)

tags:
  integration:

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text:
# Weekly CLI-coverage gardener (issue #177 follow-up, reworked by #927):
# re-measures the terminal/PTY integration suites' coverage of lib/src/cli/**
# and, when it grew, files/updates an issue assigned to ai-teammate asking
# for the baseline raise. The baseline itself NO LONGER auto-commits: every
# bump of scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt lands only through a reviewed PR
# whose per-PR ratchet gate (gh-1005: ci.yml's pty-integration-linux leg,
# the single hosted-linux PTY leg) passes green, and
# each bump must be traceable to a merged PTY test with real frame
# assertions (#927 contract). The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py)
# still enforces the committed floor — coverage can only ratchet UP, a
# silent regression in terminal-test coverage reddens nightly.
name: CLI coverage gardener

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '53 4 * * 1' # Monday, after the shard rebalance
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  measure-and-file:
    name: Measure CLI coverage, file raise-to-X issue if higher
    # gh-1005: measure on the SAME environment the per-PR ratchet measures —
    # ubuntu-24.04-arm (pure-dart job per the runner-split note; OS-identical
    # line hits to the x64 queue).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Run PTY/CLI integration suites with coverage
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
          OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage

      - run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: File coverage-growth issue when measured exceeds baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          measured=$(python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --print | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          baseline=$(cat scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt)
          echo "measured=$measured baseline=$baseline"
          if ! python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$measured') > float('$baseline') else 1)"; then
            echo "No growth — baseline stays $baseline"
            exit 0
          fi
          title="raise coverage to $measured"
          body="$(printf 'Weekly CLI-coverage gardener measured **%s**%% on lib/src/cli/** — above the committed floor of **%s**%% (scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt).\n\nPer the #927 contract the baseline never auto-commits: land the raise through a reviewed PR that\n- updates scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt to %s,\n- passes the per-PR pty-integration-linux ratchet gate green, and\n- traces every bump to a merged PTY test with real frame assertions.\n' "$measured" "$baseline" "$measured")"
          number=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --search "in:title \"raise coverage to\"" --json number,createdAt --jq 'sort_by(.createdAt) | map(.number) | last // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$number" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "updated issue #$number"
          else
            # The #927 AC wants the raise-to-X issue assigned to ai-teammate;
            # keep the measured number alive even when the login is not
            # assignable (renamed/removed) — file unassigned as a fallback.
            gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --assignee ai-teammate --title "$title" --body "$body" ||
              gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "filed raise-to-$measured issue"
          fi

- name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json

      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an

      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          # The installer writes version.txt into the bundle; mirror it so
          # `fa --version` from the AOT binary reports the real version
          # (the _packageVersion() fallback chain reads bundle/version.txt).
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
pr_base_branch.txt

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text:
# Weekly CLI-coverage gardener (issue #177 follow-up, reworked by #927):
# re-measures the terminal/PTY integration suites' coverage of lib/src/cli/**
# and, when it grew, files/updates an issue assigned to ai-teammate asking
# for the baseline raise. The baseline itself NO LONGER auto-commits: every
# bump of scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt lands only through a reviewed PR
# whose per-PR ratchet gate (gh-1005: ci.yml's pty-integration-linux leg,
# the single hosted-linux PTY leg) passes green, and
# each bump must be traceable to a merged PTY test with real frame
# assertions (#927 contract). The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py)
# still enforces the committed floor — coverage can only ratchet UP, a
# silent regression in terminal-test coverage reddens nightly.
name: CLI coverage gardener

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '53 4 * * 1' # Monday, after the shard rebalance
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  measure-and-file:
    name: Measure CLI coverage, file raise-to-X issue if higher
    # gh-1005: measure on the SAME environment the per-PR ratchet measures —
    # ubuntu-24.04-arm (pure-dart job per the runner-split note; OS-identical
    # line hits to the x64 queue).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Run PTY/CLI integration suites with coverage
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
          OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage

      - run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: File coverage-growth issue when measured exceeds baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          measured=$(python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --print | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          baseline=$(cat scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt)
          echo "measured=$measured baseline=$baseline"
          if ! python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$measured') > float('$baseline') else 1)"; then
            echo "No growth — baseline stays $baseline"
            exit 0
          fi
          title="raise coverage to $measured"
          body="$(printf 'Weekly CLI-coverage gardener measured **%s**%% on lib/src/cli/** — above the committed floor of **%s**%% (scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt).\n\nPer the #927 contract the baseline never auto-commits: land the raise through a reviewed PR that\n- updates scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt to %s,\n- passes the per-PR pty-integration-linux ratchet gate green, and\n- traces every bump to a merged PTY test with real frame assertions.\n' "$measured" "$baseline" "$measured")"
          number=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --search "in:title \"raise coverage to\"" --json number,createdAt --jq 'sort_by(.createdAt) | map(.number) | last // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$number" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "updated issue #$number"
          else
            # The #927 AC wants the raise-to-X issue assigned to ai-teammate;
            # keep the measured number alive even when the login is not
            # assignable (renamed/removed) — file unassigned as a fallback.
            gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --assignee ai-teammate --title "$title" --body "$body" ||
              gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "filed raise-to-$measured issue"
          fi

- name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text:
# Weekly CLI-coverage gardener (issue #177 follow-up, reworked by #927):
# re-measures the terminal/PTY integration suites' coverage of lib/src/cli/**
# and, when it grew, files/updates an issue assigned to ai-teammate asking
# for the baseline raise. The baseline itself NO LONGER auto-commits: every
# bump of scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt lands only through a reviewed PR
# whose per-PR ratchet gate (gh-1005: ci.yml's pty-integration-linux leg,
# the single hosted-linux PTY leg) passes green, and
# each bump must be traceable to a merged PTY test with real frame
# assertions (#927 contract). The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py)
# still enforces the committed floor — coverage can only ratchet UP, a
# silent regression in terminal-test coverage reddens nightly.
name: CLI coverage gardener

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '53 4 * * 1' # Monday, after the shard rebalance
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  measure-and-file:
    name: Measure CLI coverage, file raise-to-X issue if higher
    # gh-1005: measure on the SAME environment the per-PR ratchet measures —
    # ubuntu-24.04-arm (pure-dart job per the runner-split note; OS-identical
    # line hits to the x64 queue).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Run PTY/CLI integration suites with coverage
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
          OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage

      - run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: File coverage-growth issue when measured exceeds baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          measured=$(python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --print | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          baseline=$(cat scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt)
          echo "measured=$measured baseline=$baseline"
          if ! python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$measured') > float('$baseline') else 1)"; then
            echo "No growth — baseline stays $baseline"
            exit 0
          fi
          title="raise coverage to $measured"
          body="$(printf 'Weekly CLI-coverage gardener measured **%s**%% on lib/src/cli/** — above the committed floor of **%s**%% (scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt).\n\nPer the #927 contract the baseline never auto-commits: land the raise through a reviewed PR that\n- updates scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt to %s,\n- passes the per-PR pty-integration-linux ratchet gate green, and\n- traces every bump to a merged PTY test with real frame assertions.\n' "$measured" "$baseline" "$measured")"
          number=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --search "in:title \"raise coverage to\"" --json number,createdAt --jq 'sort_by(.createdAt) | map(.number) | last // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$number" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "updated issue #$number"
          else
            # The #927 AC wants the raise-to-X issue assigned to ai-teammate;
            # keep the measured number alive even when the login is not
            # assignable (renamed/removed) — file unassigned as a fallback.
            gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --assignee ai-teammate --title "$title" --body "$body" ||
              gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "filed raise-to-$measured issue"
          fi

- name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          # The installer writes version.txt into the bundle; mirror it so
          # `fa --version` from the AOT binary reports the real version
          # (the _packageVersion() fallback chain reads bundle/version.txt).
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # PR runs stamp from git describe (falls back to the short sha
          # on shallow checkouts); release runs get the exact tag from the
          # release binaries job.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text:
# Weekly CLI-coverage gardener (issue #177 follow-up, reworked by #927):
# re-measures the terminal/PTY integration suites' coverage of lib/src/cli/**
# and, when it grew, files/updates an issue assigned to ai-teammate asking
# for the baseline raise. The baseline itself NO LONGER auto-commits: every
# bump of scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt lands only through a reviewed PR
# whose per-PR ratchet gate (gh-1005: ci.yml's pty-integration-linux leg,
# the single hosted-linux PTY leg) passes green, and
# each bump must be traceable to a merged PTY test with real frame
# assertions (#927 contract). The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py)
# still enforces the committed floor — coverage can only ratchet UP, a
# silent regression in terminal-test coverage reddens nightly.
name: CLI coverage gardener

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '53 4 * * 1' # Monday, after the shard rebalance
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  measure-and-file:
    name: Measure CLI coverage, file raise-to-X issue if higher
    # gh-1005: measure on the SAME environment the per-PR ratchet measures —
    # ubuntu-24.04-arm (pure-dart job per the runner-split note; OS-identical
    # line hits to the x64 queue).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Run PTY/CLI integration suites with coverage
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
          OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage

      - run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: File coverage-growth issue when measured exceeds baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          measured=$(python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --print | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          baseline=$(cat scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt)
          echo "measured=$measured baseline=$baseline"
          if ! python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$measured') > float('$baseline') else 1)"; then
            echo "No growth — baseline stays $baseline"
            exit 0
          fi
          title="raise coverage to $measured"
          body="$(printf 'Weekly CLI-coverage gardener measured **%s**%% on lib/src/cli/** — above the committed floor of **%s**%% (scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt).\n\nPer the #927 contract the baseline never auto-commits: land the raise through a reviewed PR that\n- updates scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt to %s,\n- passes the per-PR pty-integration-linux ratchet gate green, and\n- traces every bump to a merged PTY test with real frame assertions.\n' "$measured" "$baseline" "$measured")"
          number=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --search "in:title \"raise coverage to\"" --json number,createdAt --jq 'sort_by(.createdAt) | map(.number) | last // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$number" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "updated issue #$number"
          else
            # The #927 AC wants the raise-to-X issue assigned to ai-teammate;
            # keep the measured number alive even when the login is not
            # assignable (renamed/removed) — file unassigned as a fallback.
            gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --assignee ai-teammate --title "$title" --body "$body" ||
              gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "filed raise-to-$measured issue"
          fi

- name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json

      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an

      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          # The installer writes version.txt into the bundle; mirror it so
          # `fa --version` from the AOT binary reports the real version
          # (the _packageVersion() fallback chain reads bundle/version.txt).
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text:
# Weekly CLI-coverage gardener (issue #177 follow-up, reworked by #927):
# re-measures the terminal/PTY integration suites' coverage of lib/src/cli/**
# and, when it grew, files/updates an issue assigned to ai-teammate asking
# for the baseline raise. The baseline itself NO LONGER auto-commits: every
# bump of scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt lands only through a reviewed PR
# whose per-PR ratchet gate (gh-1005: ci.yml's pty-integration-linux leg,
# the single hosted-linux PTY leg) passes green, and
# each bump must be traceable to a merged PTY test with real frame
# assertions (#927 contract). The nightly ratchet (check_cli_coverage.py)
# still enforces the committed floor — coverage can only ratchet UP, a
# silent regression in terminal-test coverage reddens nightly.
name: CLI coverage gardener

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '53 4 * * 1' # Monday, after the shard rebalance
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  measure-and-file:
    name: Measure CLI coverage, file raise-to-X issue if higher
    # gh-1005: measure on the SAME environment the per-PR ratchet measures —
    # ubuntu-24.04-arm (pure-dart job per the runner-split note; OS-identical
    # line hits to the x64 queue).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Run PTY/CLI integration suites with coverage
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
          OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage

      - run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: File coverage-growth issue when measured exceeds baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          measured=$(python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --print | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          baseline=$(cat scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt)
          echo "measured=$measured baseline=$baseline"
          if ! python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$measured') > float('$baseline') else 1)"; then
            echo "No growth — baseline stays $baseline"
            exit 0
          fi
          title="raise coverage to $measured"
          body="$(printf 'Weekly CLI-coverage gardener measured **%s**%% on lib/src/cli/** — above the committed floor of **%s**%% (scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt).\n\nPer the #927 contract the baseline never auto-commits: land the raise through a reviewed PR that\n- updates scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt to %s,\n- passes the per-PR pty-integration-linux ratchet gate green, and\n- traces every bump to a merged PTY test with real frame assertions.\n' "$measured" "$baseline" "$measured")"
          number=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --search "in:title \"raise coverage to\"" --json number,createdAt --jq 'sort_by(.createdAt) | map(.number) | last // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$number" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "updated issue #$number"
          else
            # The #927 AC wants the raise-to-X issue assigned to ai-teammate;
            # keep the measured number alive even when the login is not
            # assignable (renamed/removed) — file unassigned as a fallback.
            gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --assignee ai-teammate --title "$title" --body "$body" ||
              gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --title "$title" --body "$body"
            echo "filed raise-to-$measured issue"
          fi

        with:
